assays.assay_description: C57BL/6J mice received s.c. injections of 4-MeO-MiPT and related tryptamine analogs (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle and were video-recorded (GoPro, 120 fps) for 30 min post-injection in TruScan testing chambers. HTR events were quantified via a DeepLabCut pose-estimation + SimBA random-forest classifier pipeline; dose-response and within-session time-course curves were generated. Variants included fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) or WAY100635 (3 mg/kg) pretreatment 10 min before test drug (all collapsed into one assay).

application_type.evidence: mice received subcutaneous injection of either drug (0.03-30 mg/kg) or vehicle (saline or 90:5:5 saline:DMSO:Tween 80)

setup_habituation.evidence: baseline temperature for each mouse was recorded after brief acclimation to testing chambers — within-session acclimation only; no separate prior habituation session described

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in the testing chamber and behavior was video recorded for 30 min postinjection; no restraint described.

outcomes.summary: Tryptamine analogs produced dose-related increases in head twitches over a 30 min session (ED50 range 0.09-10.53 mg/kg; Emax 20-98 HTRs/30 min), typically with bell-shaped dose-response curves. 4-MeO analogs induced fewer HTRs than their 4-OH counterparts (e.g., miprocin Emax = 70 vs 4-MeO-MiPT Emax = 39 HTRs/30 min), and fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) pretreatment reduced the maximal HTRs evoked by miprocin, 4-HO-DiPT and 4-HO-McPT to levels comparable to the 4-MeO analogs; WAY100635 pretreatment increased HTRs at the high (30 mg/kg) dose of 4-MeO-MiPT. Several compounds (4-MeO-DMT, 4-MeO-NiPT, 4-MeO-sBuT, 4-MeO-3PT) were HTR inactive.
outcomes.statistics: Comparisons of dose-response data for acute drug effects (HTR, body temperature change) were conducted via Welch's ANOVA followed by Dunnett's T3 post hoc analyses comparing all groups to vehicle controls; in antagonist/pretreatment studies, dose-by-dose comparisons used two-way ANOVA (dose × treatment) with Sidak's post hoc test; alpha = 0.05. (Numerical statistics in Tables S3 and S5.)
outcomes.evidence: Compared to miprocin, 4-MeO-MiPT induced less HTRs with slightly weaker potency (ED50 = 0.76 vs 0.97 mg/kg, Emax = 70 vs 39 HTR/30 min)... FLX pretreatment prior to 4-HO-DiPT and 4-HO-McPT reduced the maximal number of HTRs.

B1_num_measures.evidence: The sole behavioural variable reported is the number of head twitch responses (HTRs/30 min); body temperature is a physiological, not behavioural, measure and locomotor activity was 'data not shown'.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time-course plots for HTR counts induced by the selected compounds (G-J)... '4-HO-McPT produced peak HTR counts in the first 5 min postinjection which resolved within 15-20 min'

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions, sequences or bout microstructure reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: The endpoint is the head twitch response, which the rubric explicitly excludes from ethological behaviours.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested individually in HTR chambers; no social construct measured.

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR is an innate drug-induced response requiring no learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Pose estimation models were trained using DLC version 2.3.10. Behavioral classifiers were generated using SimBA version 2.2.4 (random forest models; precision = 95.93, recall = 93.74).

B8_multivariate.evidence: No PCA/UMAP/clustering of behavioural features reported; analyses are univariate dose-response comparisons.

E1_environment_type.evidence: The approximate width of the TruScan chamber was used to define pixels per mm during the Video Settings step.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter or refuge described in the TruScan testing chamber.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material described in the testing chamber.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects described in the testing chamber.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each mouse was recorded individually in its testing chamber for 30 min postinjection.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described within the 30 min testing chamber session.

D1_continuity.evidence: Drug treatments occurred every 1-2 weeks to avoid tolerance — indicating repeated 30-min HTR recording sessions in the same animals across the dose-response and pretreatment studies.

D2_session_duration.evidence: behavior was video recorded with Hero 7 GoPro cameras ... for 30 min postinjection

D3_recording_days.evidence: Drug treatments occurred every 1-2 weeks to avoid tolerance (repeated test days per animal); the exact number of test days is not stated.

D4_baseline.evidence: Only baseline body temperature was recorded before injection ('baseline temperature for each mouse was recorded after brief acclimation to testing chambers'); no pre-drug behavioural HTR data reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Behaviour was recorded only for 30 min postinjection; no recording ≥24 h after dosing.

D6_circadian.evidence: Sessions lasted 30 min, far less than 6 h.

judge_notes: Only one behavioural assay in the paper: the mouse head twitch response (HTR). All in vitro work (binding, BRET, calcium mobilization, synaptosome uptake/release, Tango) was excluded as non-behavioural.

Body temperature change was excluded as a purely physiological measure, so B1 counts only HTR counts (score 0, '1 measure'); gemma4's B1 score of 1 with value '1' was internally inconsistent and overridden.

Dose-response arms, fluoxetine pretreatment, and WAY100635 pretreatment were merged into the single HTR assay per the rubric's 'same test with different pharmacological antagonists/doses = 1 assay' rule.
Locomotor activity was monitored during the same sessions but reported as 'data not shown', so it was not scored as a separate assay or as an additional behavioural measure.

D1/D3: scored 'Multiple discrete sessions' and '2-7 days' based on the explicit statement that drug treatments occurred every 1-2 weeks to avoid tolerance (repeated within-subject testing); exact day counts are not given, hence medium confidence.

Dose arrays left empty because the paper reports only a range (0.03-30 mg/kg), not discrete dose values; fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) and WAY100635 (3 mg/kg) added as additional dosing entries missed by all candidates.
